votes.title: Keith Sonderling for Secretary of Labor
votes.sum: Confirmed Keith Sonderling of Florida to lead the Department of Labor, which enforces wage, workplace-safety, and retirement-plan rules.

votes.title: Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)
votes.q: Cloture on the motion to proceed · 60 votes needed
votes.sum: Would require electric utilities serving very large customers (peak loads of 100 megawatts or more, such as data centers) to set rates so those customers pay the full cost of grid upgrades built for them, backed by financial guarantees. The vote to begin debate fell 3 short of 60.
votes.related: The House passed this bill 417–3 on Sep 16 (House roll 312).

votes.title: Stop Insider Trading Act (H.R. 7008)
votes.q: Cloture on the motion to proceed · 60 votes needed
votes.sum: Would bar members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from buying new individual stocks. It would not require them to sell stocks they already own. Supporters called it a ban on congressional insider trading; Democrats who opposed it called it weaker than other bipartisan proposals and objected to provisions added to the Senate package, which press coverage said included a federal voter ID requirement. The vote split along party lines.
votes.caution: This package reportedly also included a voter ID requirement, and opponents said the stock limits were too weak. A No vote may not mean opposition to limiting stock trading.

votes.title: College athlete name, image & likeness bill (S. 4668)
votes.sum: Sets national rules protecting college athletes' rights to earn money from their name, image, and likeness, with added protections for athletes and rules meant to keep competition among schools fair. Passed with support from both parties.

votes.title: Iran war powers resolution (H.Con.Res. 89)
votes.sum: Would have directed the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran. Failed by one vote.
votes.related: The House passed a similar resolution, H.Con.Res. 93, on Sep 15 (House roll 307).

votes.title: Photo ID to vote in federal elections (S. 5271)
votes.q: Cloture on the motion to proceed · 60 votes needed
votes.sum: Would amend the Help America Vote Act to require voters to show photo identification in federal elections. The vote to begin debate fell 8 short of 60.

votes.title: Stopgap government funding for FY2027 (H.R. 6500)
votes.sum: A continuing resolution that funds the federal government at current levels into fiscal year 2027 and extends several expiring programs, avoiding a shutdown while full-year spending bills are negotiated.

votes.title: Russia sanctions bill (H.R. 5334)
votes.sum: Imposes new sanctions on Russia, including duties on countries that buy Russian oil or gas or help Russia evade sanctions. Named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.
votes.related: The House agreed to the Senate's version 262–159 on Sep 16 (House roll 308).

votes.title: Housing supply bill (H.R. 6644)
votes.q: Motion to concur in the House amendment, with an amendment
votes.sum: A broad bill aimed at increasing the number of homes built in the United States. This vote sent the Senate's final version back to the House.

votes.title: Budget reconciliation bill (S. 2)
votes.sum: A party-line budget bill passed under rules that need only a simple majority. It provides roughly $70 billion for ICE and border protection and lowers the funding cap for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Passed after an overnight series of amendment votes.
votes.caution: This bill covered more than border funding, including changes to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, so a vote on it reflects the whole package.

votes.title: Retire through Ownership Act (S. 2403)
votes.q: Suspend the rules and pass · two-thirds needed
votes.sum: Clarifies how trustees of employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs) value the stock of privately held companies, letting them rely on an independent, qualified appraisal that follows IRS valuation standards. Backers say this reduces legal risk for companies that want to set up or keep employee ownership plans. Passed with wide support from both parties, sending the bill to the President.
votes.related: The Senate passed this bill unanimously on Oct 9, 2025.

votes.title: Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (H.R. 9497)
votes.q: Suspend the rules and pass, as amended · two-thirds needed
votes.sum: Authorizes Army Corps of Engineers water projects and studies for navigation, flood control, and water supply, including 10 new construction projects and 131 new feasibility studies. It also creates new Corps programs for drought resilience and flood-risk management and an online system for tracking permit applications. Passed with wide support from both parties; the Senate has its own version (S. 4949).

votes.title: Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)
votes.q: Suspend the rules and pass · two-thirds needed
votes.sum: Would require electric utilities serving very large customers (100 megawatts or more, such as data centers) to set rates so those customers pay the full cost of grid upgrades built for them. Nearly unanimous.
votes.related: Stalled in the Senate on Sep 30 when a vote to begin debate got 57 of the 60 votes needed.

votes.title: PROOF Act (H.R. 10326)
votes.sum: Lets state administrators of major federal benefit programs share program data with the Attorney General to investigate and prosecute fraud, with encryption, data-destruction, and Privacy Act safeguards, and requires a report to Congress on resulting investigations and convictions. Passed mostly along party lines.

votes.title: Russia sanctions bill (H.R. 5334)
votes.q: Motion to concur in the Senate amendments
votes.sum: Accepted the Senate's version of the Russia sanctions bill, which adds duties on countries that buy Russian oil or gas or help Russia evade sanctions.
votes.related: The Senate passed this version 86–11 on Aug 7 (Senate roll 224).

votes.title: Iran war powers resolution (H.Con.Res. 93)
votes.sum: Directs the President, under the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran. All Democrats present and 7 Republicans voted yes.
votes.related: The Senate rejected a similar resolution, H.Con.Res. 89, 49–50 on Sep 24.
